scenarios.prompt: Two-arm A/B test (control vs variant). Control: 312 conversions out of 4,800 visitors. Variant: 358 conversions out of 4,750 visitors. Compute the two-proportion two-sided z-test. Report p1, p2, z_statistic, p_value_two_sided, and cohens_h. The test should be significant at alpha=0.05 but only barely.

Control: 540 conversions out of 10,000. Variant: 590 conversions out of 10,000. The relative lift is 9.3%, which sounds material — but is the difference statistically significant at alpha=0.05? Compute the two-proportion two-sided z-test and report p1, p2, z_statistic, p_value_two_sided, cohens_h.

Control: 100,200 conversions out of 2,000,000 visitors. Variant: 100,600 conversions out of 2,000,000 visitors. Compute the two-proportion two-sided z-test. Report p1, p2, z_statistic, p_value_two_sided, and cohens_h. (This is the classic 'huge sample, trivial effect' case — pay attention to whether the test is significant AND whether the effect size is meaningful.)
